newsitem.title: MALI: MALI STUDENTS CLASH WITH POLICE IN POLL RUN-UP.
newsitem.headline: MALI STUDENTS CLASH WITH POLICE IN POLL RUN-UP.

text.p: Security forces fired teargas at stone-throwing students who burned posters of Mali's President Alpha Oumar Konare in the capital Bamako on Tuesday ahead of a contentious presidential election, witnesses said.

"The students went wild, they were burning tyres in the streets...the city centre was paralysed until early afternoon when the police cleared them," said one witness. She added that five children had been lightly injured and 10 arrested.

School and university students burned posters and banners of Konare, who stands for re-election on Sunday in the impoverished West African country's second multi-party presidential election since independence in 1960.

The students, who were protesting against a slow and chaotic start to the school year, also demanded the departure of Konare, whose insistence on keeping a May 11 date for the presidential poll has outraged opposition supporters.
A strike by some public sector workers deprived the capital of both electricity and water.
Widespread praise greeted Mali's 1992 transition from single-party dictatorship to multi-party democracy.

But serious organisational problems disrupted last month's parliamentary elections, during which Malians turned out in force only to be frustrated by lack of ballot papers and problems with voter cards and lists.
The constitutional court in the former French colony scrapped the results citing irregularities although a date for a new ballot has not yet been set.
Opposition parties called on the constitutional court to scrap the decree allowing Sunday's vote to go ahead. Konare, who has delayed the elections by a week, says they must go ahead this time.
The court has yet to rule on the opposition's appeal.
Three members of the independent electoral commission said on Tuesday they had written to Konare asking for the elections to be postponed to allow better organisation.
Mamadou Dante, one of those who signed the letter, said the call was made in the name of non-political interest groups that the three represent on the 30-member commission.
"In the public interest we have asked for a review of dates for better organised elections," Dante, a lawyer, told Reuters.
The only challenger to Konare is businessman Hamadou Maribatrou Diaby.
